payload.reasoning:
Because ∠CHB = 90° (altitude ⊥ AB) and ∠HBC = β in right triangle BHC, ∠HCB = 90° − β. Since X lies on segment CH, ∠XCB = ∠HCB = 90° − β. In triangle BXC:
∠BXC = 180° − (β/2) − (90° − β) = 90° + β/2.

Since O and X are both inside the acute triangle, they are on the same side of line BC. Therefore in the circle through B, O, X, C, both O and X lie on the same arc with respect to chord BC, so the inscribed angles satisfy ∠BOC = ∠BXC:
2n = 90 + β/2  ⇒  4n − β = 180  ⇒  β = 4n − 180.

Combined with n + β + γ = 180:
γ = 180 − n − (4n − 180) = 360 − 5n.

Acute triangle requires each angle strictly less than 90°:
• β = 4n − 180 < 90  ⇒  n < 67.5
• γ = 360 − 5n < 90  ⇒  n > 54
• β > 0  ⇒  n > 45
• n < 90

So 54 < n < 67.5. The largest positive integer in this range is n = 67.

Check: n = 67 gives β = 88, γ = 25; sum is 180; all angles acute. ✓
Check n = 68: β = 92 (obtuse), so the triangle is not acute. ✗
